C1.name: FRC.Observation.power_maps
C1.doc: 22:C1 — the characters of the Object cycle are the power maps `u ↦ u^k`: each is multiplicative, and for a cycle generated by `ζ` of order `n` the maps of distinct windings `k, k' < n` differ (at the generator).

C1.name: FRC.Observation.roots_of_order
C1.doc: 22:C1 — every `n`-th root of unity is a power of a given element of order `n` (the root bound of `Xⁿ − 1`; the proof of `FRC.Quantum.absorbed` with the generator replaced by any element of order `n`).

C1.name: FRC.Observation.character_is_power_map
C1.doc: 22:C1 — the characters are the power maps: a multiplicative map `χ` on the cycle `⟨ζ⟩` of order `n` (`χ(ζ^a ζ^b) = χ(ζ^a) χ(ζ^b)`, `χ 1 = 1`) is `u ↦ u^k` for one `k < n`, `χ(ζ^j) = (ζ^j)^k` for every `j`.

C2.name: FRC.Observation.stationary
C2.doc: 22:C2 — the windings are the drive's eigenvectors: `ψ_k(g u) = g^k ψ_k(u)`, the eigenvalue `g^k` is the weight `k` per chronon, and the eigenvalues of the windings `k < n` are distinct for a drive `g` of order `n` on the cycle.

C2.name: FRC.Observation.stationary_modes
C2.doc: 22:C2 — the stationary states are the winding modes: a function `ψ` on the cycle `⟨g⟩` of order `n` that the drive scales, `ψ(g · g^j) = λ ψ(g^j)` for every `j`, is `ψ(g^j) = ψ(1) (g^j)^k` for one winding `k < n` with `λ = g^k` when `ψ 1 ≠ 0`, and vanishes on the cycle when `ψ 1 = 0`.

C3.name: FRC.Observation.orthogonality
C3.doc: 00:F4, 00:F6, 22:C3, 22:X3 — orthogonality of the forced basis: for a core `C_d` generated by `ω`, the characters `η_r(j) = ω^{rj}` satisfy `Σ_{j<d} η_r(j) η_{r'}(j)⁻¹ = d δ_{rr'}` (the inverse character is `ω^{(d−r')j}`).

C3.name: FRC.Observation.parseval
C3.doc: 00:F4, 22:C3, 22:C7 — the bilinear Parseval identity on the core: for any two coefficient vectors `f, g` on the fibre, `Σ_{r<d} (Σ_j f_j ω^{(d−r)j}) (Σ_l g_l ω^{rl}) = d Σ_j f_j g_j` (with `g = f̄` the resolution of identity and the norm identity of the forced basis).

C3.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.fourier_inversion
C3.doc: 00:C11 (iii), 22:C3, 22:C12 — Fourier inversion recovers every coefficient exactly: `Σ_d K(d) i^{−rd} = 4 c_r`.

C3.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.dft_det
C3.doc: 00:C11 (v), 22:C3, 22:C12 — the core DFT matrix `(i^{ru})` is invertible: its determinant is `−16i`.

C4.name: FRC.Observation.selection
C4.doc: 00:F4, 00:F6, 22:C4, 22:C23, 22:X3, 22:C24, 22:X5 — the selection rule: a pointer channel `r < d` couples to the Object winding `k` over a fibre of the core exactly when their core phases agree, `k ≡ r (mod d)`: `Σ_{j<d} ω^{kj} ω^{(d−r)j} = d [k ≡ r]`.

C5.name: FRC.Observation.lueders
C5.doc: 00:F4, 22:C5, 22:X4 — the Lüders projector of the channel `r`, `Π_{jl} = ω^{rj} ω^{(d−r)l}`, is idempotent up to `d`: `Π² = d Π`, so an immediately repeated registration returns the outcome.

C6.name: FRC.Observation.frobenius_unique
C6.doc: 22:C6 — the Frobenius is forced: a ring map `σ` of `𝔽_{p²}` fixing the shell (`σ(c) = c`, additive, multiplicative) is the identity or the conjugation `w ↦ −w`, since `σ(w)² = ν` leaves `σ(w) = ±w`.

C6.name: FRC.Observation.torus_conj_inv
C6.doc: 22:C6, 22:P4 — on the norm-one torus the conjugation is the inversion: `z · conj z = 1`.

C6.name: FRC.Observation.exponent_negation
C6.doc: 22:C6 — exponent negation inverts the phase cycle: `ζ^{n−k}` is the inverse of `ζ^k` on a cycle of order `n`.

C7.name: FRC.Observation.pair_count
C7.doc: 22:C7, 22:X1 — the pair count: the squared amplitude is the double sum of phase agreements, `(Σ_j ψ_j)(Σ_l ψ̄_l) = Σ_j Σ_l ψ_j ψ̄_l`.

C7.name: FRC.Observation.pure_winding_weight
C7.doc: 22:C7, 22:C10, 22:X1 — on a pure winding `k` the weight of the channel `r < d` is `d² [k ≡ r (mod d)]`: the amplitude `Σ_j ω^{kj} ω^{(d−r)j}` times its conjugate `Σ_l ω^{rl} ω^{(d−k)l}` (the conjugate winding `d − k % d`).

C7.name: FRC.Observation.parseval
C7.doc: 00:F4, 22:C3, 22:C7 — the bilinear Parseval identity on the core: for any two coefficient vectors `f, g` on the fibre, `Σ_{r<d} (Σ_j f_j ω^{(d−r)j}) (Σ_l g_l ω^{rl}) = d Σ_j f_j g_j` (with `g = f̄` the resolution of identity and the norm identity of the forced basis).

C7.name: FRC.Quantum.dephasing
C7.doc: 00:F2, 00:F6, 22:C26, 22:C7 — dephasing is exact: on a prime shell `q`, a character `χ(x) = Π_j ζ_j^{x_j}` of the composite (`ζ_j^{n_j} = 1`) that the drive moves (`χ(v) = Π_j ζ_j ≠ 1`) sums to zero along the drive, `Σ_{t<M} χ(t v) = 0`, over every joint recurrence `M`, the product of the periods among them.

C7.name: FRC.Quantum.pair_count_tally
C7.doc: 22:C7, 22:X1 — the ledger weight `z z̄ = N(z)` is a nonnegative integer, the coincidence count (`FRC.QuantumML.pair_count_tally`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C8.name: FRC.Interference.sorkin_hierarchy
C8.doc: 22:C8, 22:X8, 22:P2 — **the Sorkin hierarchy**: for every additive conjugation `c`, every family of paths `a` and every base point `x`, the `k`-fold mixed difference of the weight `w(x) = x c(x)` is zero for every `k ≥ 3`; so the interference terms `I_k = Δ_{a_{k−1}} ⋯ Δ_{a_0} w (0)` vanish exactly from the third order on, on every channel and outcome (the ledger's value reduces to the shadow, and a vanishing shadow lifts to a multiple of `Ω`).

C8.name: FRC.Interference.sorkin_second
C8.doc: 22:C8 — the second difference is the cross term: `Δ_b Δ_a w (x) = b c(a) + a c(b)`, independent of `x`.

C8.name: FRC.Interference.sorkin_second_witness
C8.doc: 22:C8 — `I₂` is generically nonzero: with `c` the identity and the paths `a = b = 1`, `I₂ = 2 ≠ 0` on every shell `q > 2`.

C8.name: FRC.Quantum.sorkin_hierarchy
C8.doc: 22:C8, 22:X8, 22:P2 — the Sorkin hierarchy on every commutative ring with an additive conjugation (`FRC.QuantumML.sorkin_hierarchy`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C8.name: FRC.Quantum.sorkin_second_witness
C8.doc: 22:C8 — `I₂` is generically nonzero on the ledger: on `ℤ[i]` with the conjugation and the paths `a = b = 1`, `I₂ = 2` (`FRC.QuantumML.sorkin_second_witness`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C9.name: FRC.Observation.reduce_add
C9.doc: 22:C9 — the reduction is additive: the shadow of `c + c'` is the sum of the shadows.

C9.name: FRC.Observation.reduce_mul
C9.doc: 22:C9, 22:C17 — the reduction is multiplicative: with `v^n = 1`, the shadow of the convolution `c ⋆ c'` is the product of the shadows; the Carrier-chart amplitude of a product is the product of the amplitudes, exact as algebra.

C9.name: FRC.Observation.reduce_wrap
C9.doc: 22:C9 — the reduction is silent about magnitude: the count `q` itself reduces to `0`.

C10.name: FRC.Extension.two_way_tally
C10.doc: 00:C10 (S1), 22:C10, 22:X1 — the part of the extension fixed by its conjugation is the tally line: a weight `z` is its own conjugate exactly when its `w`-component vanishes (the frame's odd prime), and the symmetrised weight `z + z̄` is the tally-line element `tr(z)`. For `ℤ[i]`, `ν = −1`, this is the paper's two-way subring.

C10.name: FRC.Extension.core_weights
C10.doc: 00:C10 (S2, S4), 22:C10 — the engineered-core weights reduce to the core: `W₊ + W₋ = 4` and `W₊ W₋ = 2` in every `𝔽_p[w]/(w² − 2)`, and on `Ω = 641` (`641 ≡ 1 (mod 8)`) as residues, `r = 67`, `r² = 2`, `W± = 2 ± r`, with `r` a grid point of the Subject chart of generator `3`, `r = 3⁵⁵⁵` (S4).

C10.name: FRC.Extension.root_two_two_way
C10.doc: 00:C10 (S2), 22:C10 — the two-way root of two: on a frame, for `ζ` of order `8` (`ζ⁸ = 1`, `ζ⁴ ≠ 1`) and `η = ζ⁻¹`, `(ζ + η)² = 2`. So `w = ζ₈ + ζ₈⁻¹` lies in the paper's two-way subring, the part of the cyclotomic ring fixed by `ζ ↦ ζ⁻¹`, and the engineered-core weights `2 ± w` are two-way (on `641`: `ζ₈ = 318`, `ζ₈ + ζ₈⁻¹ = 574 = −67`).

C10.name: FRC.Extension.framed_readout
C10.doc: 00:C10 (S5–S7), 22:C10, 22:C11, 22:X6 — a registered probability is a framed rational, decided by the kernel: the grid bound `s_n² ≤ 2 · 9ⁿ < (s_n + 1)²` at every scale `n ≤ 8` and the readouts nest, `3 s_n ≤ s_{n+1} ≤ 3 s_n + 2`; the readout `R_4((2 + √2)/8) = (2 · 3⁴ + 114)/(8 · 3⁴) = 23/54`; the `√3` instance `s_3 = 46`; the largest-remainder allocation at `B = 81` of `(23/54, 23/54, 4/54, 4/54)` is `35 + 34 + 6 + 6` (the floors `34 + 34 + 6 + 6`, the one seat left to the first of the two remainders `27/54`). A readout computation over the naturals of the laboratory host (decision Q20).

C10.name: FRC.Observation.window_lift
C10.doc: 22:C10, 22:X1, 22:X6 — the unique window lift: two tallies below the window `Ω` with one shadow are equal, so a sub-horizon tally is the unique lift of its residue.

C10.name: FRC.Observation.pure_winding_weight
C10.doc: 22:C7, 22:C10, 22:X1 — on a pure winding `k` the weight of the channel `r < d` is `d² [k ≡ r (mod d)]`: the amplitude `Σ_j ω^{kj} ω^{(d−r)j}` times its conjugate `Σ_l ω^{rl} ω^{(d−k)l}` (the conjugate winding `d − k % d`).

C10.name: FRC.Quantum.joint_recurrence
C10.doc: 00:F2, 22:C26, 22:C10, 22:C20 — the joint recurrence of an unequal-cycle composite, found below a common multiple `L > 0` of the periods (on a shell, a joint return below `Ω`): the chronons at which all `m` parts return are exactly the multiples of one period `T`, `0 < T ≤ L`, which divides `L`. The search never passes `L` (Q20).

C11.name: FRC.Extension.conjugate_pair_tally
C11.doc: 00:C10 (S9), 22:C11 — the conjugate-pair trace tally: a flip-summed pair of conjugate string weights is core-valued, `z^k z̄^(k+m) + z̄^k z^(k+m) = N(z)^k · tr(z^m)` on the tally line, for every weight `z` of every quadratic extension.

C11.name: FRC.Extension.dial_shift
C11.doc: 00:C10 (S9), 22:C11 — the dial-shift conjugation: on a dial of `2M` settings (`ζ^(2M) = 1`, `ζ^M ≠ 1`, `η = ζ⁻¹`), the weight at the shifted setting is the conjugate weight, `w₊(M − θ) = w₋(θ)` for `θ ≤ M` (the witness: `M = 40` in `ℤ[x]/(x⁴⁰ + 1)`, `w₊(40 − D) = w₋(D)`).

C11.name: FRC.Extension.dial_tally
C11.doc: 00:C10 (S10), 22:C11 — the dial-ensemble Parseval tally: over a dial of `N` settings closed under `ζ` (`ζ^N = 1`, `ζ² ≠ 1`, `η = ζ⁻¹`) on a frame, the weights `w±(θ) = 2 ± (ζ^θ + η^θ)` sum to `2N`, and so do the products `w₊(θ) w₋(θ)`: the cross terms cancel by the character sums (the frame: no zero divisors).

C11.name: FRC.Extension.framed_readout
C11.doc: 00:C10 (S5–S7), 22:C10, 22:C11, 22:X6 — a registered probability is a framed rational, decided by the kernel: the grid bound `s_n² ≤ 2 · 9ⁿ < (s_n + 1)²` at every scale `n ≤ 8` and the readouts nest, `3 s_n ≤ s_{n+1} ≤ 3 s_n + 2`; the readout `R_4((2 + √2)/8) = (2 · 3⁴ + 114)/(8 · 3⁴) = 23/54`; the `√3` instance `s_3 = 46`; the largest-remainder allocation at `B = 81` of `(23/54, 23/54, 4/54, 4/54)` is `35 + 34 + 6 + 6` (the floors `34 + 34 + 6 + 6`, the one seat left to the first of the two remainders `27/54`). A readout computation over the naturals of the laboratory host (decision Q20).

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.winding_fixing
C12.doc: 00:C11 (i), 22:C12 — the pure windings fix the tallies on the box `−1 ≤ c_r ≤ 3` (the naturals `a, b, c, d < 5`, cast to `ℤ` and shifted by one), which contains negative coefficients: `F(K_c, ψ_k) = 16 c_k` for every kernel of the box and every channel `k`.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.tally_criterion
C12.doc: 00:C11 (i′), 22:C12, 22:X6 — the tally criterion on the box: the pair tally of `K_c` on `ψ_k` is a tally (a nonnegative integer) iff `0 ≤ c_k` — the cone's two halves: every tally combination is tally-valued on the windings, and a kernel with a negative coefficient is excluded by its own winding.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.two_way
C12.doc: 00:C11 (ii), 22:C12 — every kernel of the cube is two-way, `K(−d) = conj K(d)`, and tally-valued on the pure windings.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.fourier_inversion
C12.doc: 00:C11 (iii), 22:C3, 22:C12 — Fourier inversion recovers every coefficient exactly: `Σ_d K(d) i^{−rd} = 4 c_r`.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.channel_selectivity
C12.doc: 00:C11 (iv), 22:C12, 22:X6 — channel-selectivity picks the ray: a kernel of the cube responds on exactly one channel iff its coefficient vector is a scaled unit vector.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.dft_det
C12.doc: 00:C11 (v), 22:C3, 22:C12 — the core DFT matrix `(i^{ru})` is invertible: its determinant is `−16i`.

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.cone_boundary
C12.doc: 00:C11 (vi), 22:C12 — the witnesses of the cone's boundary (22-quantum's U3, U5, U6a): the negative coefficient `c = (1, −1, 1, 0)` is excluded by its own winding, `F(K_c, ψ₁) = −16`; the two-way kernel `5η₁ − 2η₂ + η₃` outside the box is excluded on `ψ₂` and Fourier inversion recovers `4c = (0, 20, −8, 4)`; the fibre norm `[d = 0]` is two-way, responds `(4, 4, 4, 4)` with `4c_r = 1` on every channel (no tally combination) and fails channel-selectivity; the single character `η₁` responds `16` on its channel and `0` elsewhere, so `η₁/16` reads `1` (c = 1/16, no tally).

C12.name: FRC.Extension.Tally.linear_exclusion
C12.doc: 00:C11 (vii), 22:C12 — the minimal degree is forced (22-quantum Lemma degree): a linear functional constant on the orbit vanishes on every nontrivial winding (the complete character sums), and on the trivial winding `F(i ψ₀) = i F(ψ₀)` leaves the tally cone for every nonzero multiplier `c ≤ 4`; and the unconjugated bilinear form leaves the tally line on Gaussian-lattice states where the conjugated form of the same kernel stays on it: `B(fn, (1 + i)e₀) = 2i` against `F = 2`, `B([d = 1], e₀ + i e₁) = i`, and `B(K_(1,1,0,0), (1 + i)e₀) = 4i` against `F = 4`.

C13.name: FRC.Observation.shared_core
C13.doc: 00:F4, 22:C13, 22:X2 — the shared core of two framed shells: an element of both cycles `C_{4κ}` and `C_{4κ'}` lies in `Q₄` when the capacities are coprime (`κ a = κ' b + 1` the Bezout witness), and `Q₄` lies in every such cycle.

C13.name: FRC.Observation.no_quarter_turn
C13.doc: 22:C13, 22:X2 — a shell `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` has no quarter-turn: no `x` with `x² = −1`, since such an `x` has order `4`, which divides `p − 1` by Fermat.

C14.name: FRC.Interference.hadamard_even
C14.doc: 22:C14, 22:P5 — `2m` balanced layers give the amplitude `(1 + i)^{2m} = 2^m i^m`.

C14.name: FRC.Interference.hadamard_odd
C14.doc: 22:C14 — `2m + 1` balanced layers give the amplitude `(1 + i)^{2m+1} = 2^m i^m (1 + i)`.

C14.name: FRC.Interference.tally_norm_mono
C14.doc: 22:C14, 22:P5 — the tally norm is monotone in the depth.

C14.name: FRC.Interference.ceiling_641
C14.doc: 22:C14, 22:P5 — **the ceiling on the worked carrier** `Ω = 641`: the largest depth with `T(k) < Ω` is `k* = 8` for the unit core (`T(8) = 256`, `T(9) = 1024`), and with the Bell core `d = 8` it is `6` (`8 T(6) = 512`, `8 T(7) = 2048`).

C14.name: FRC.Quantum.gaussian_layers
C14.doc: 22:C14 — the Hadamard layers on `ℤ[i]` and the minimal denominator (`FRC.QuantumML.gaussian_layers`, `gaussian_minimal`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C14.name: FRC.Quantum.gaussian_minimal
C14.doc: 22:C14, 22:P5 — `2` does not divide `i^m (1 + i)`: the minimal denominator (`FRC.QuantumML.gaussian_minimal`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C14.name: FRC.Quantum.tally_norm_eq
C14.doc: 22:C14 — the minimal tally norm is the square of the minimal denominator, `T(k) = (2^{⌈k/2⌉})²` (`FRC.QuantumML.tally_norm_eq`, `Theme/Quantum.lean`).

C15.name: FRC.Composite.offset_invariant
C15.doc: 22:C15 — the offset vector of a cluster on `(ℤ/N)^m` is invariant under the diagonal drive by `t` chronons: in the cross form, `x_j + (x_0 + t) ≡ (x_j + t) + x_0 (mod N)`.

C15.name: FRC.Composite.cluster_offset
C15.doc: 00:F6, 22:C15, lem:mbody (i)–(ii), 22:C18 — the offset is the orbit label: two configurations `x, y` of the cluster `(ℤ/N)^m` (`0 < m`, `y` reduced) lie on one orbit of the diagonal drive exactly when their offset vectors agree, `x_j − x_0 ≡ y_j − y_0 (mod N)` for every cell `j`; the drive time `t` is a residue, `t < N`, and no drive evolution connects distinct offsets.

C15.name: FRC.Composite.locked_norm
C15.doc: lem:mbody (iii), 22:C15, 22:C22 — on the synchronised orbit the amplitudes add coherently: `Σ_{i<m} χ = m χ`, and the weight `(m χ)(m χ̄) = m²` when `χ χ̄ = 1`.

C15.name: FRC.Composite.spread_average
C15.doc: lem:mbody (iii), 22:C22, 22:C15 — **the offset-uniform average is `m`**: for `m` cells with independent uniform phases on a cycle of order `n` (`ζ` of order `n`, `η = ζ⁻¹`, neither `1`), the sum over all `n^m` configurations of `|Σ_i ζ^{v_i}|² = (Σ_i ζ^{v_i})(Σ_j η^{v_j})` is `m n^m`, the average `m`, against `m²` on the synchronised orbit: the `√m` lives only in amplitude-coherent observables.

C15.name: FRC.Quantum.pair_offset
C15.doc: 00:F2, 00:F6, 22:C26, 22:C15, 22:C18, 22:P3 — two parts of periods `a`, `b` with joint period `T` (a common multiple, and no positive common multiple below it): the number `g` with `g T = a b` divides both periods, and every common divisor divides it (`g` is the gcd); the joint drive carries `(x, y)` to `(x', y')` within one joint period exactly when the offsets agree modulo `g` — the conserved offset on the gcd cycle, the orbits the quotient `A/⟨v⟩ ≅ ℤ/g`.

C16.name: FRC.Composite.half_turn_sixteen
C16.doc: 22:C16 — an element of order `16` has `v⁸ = −1`: the half-turn supplies the sign.

C16.name: FRC.Composite.doublet_readout
C16.doc: 22:C16 — **the forced readout is `σ_x`**: on the `C_{16}` Object `⟨v⟩` read by a core-`C_8` Subject (`ω = v²` the core's generator), the doublet state `u^k + λ u^{k+8}` registers on the matched channel `r = k mod 8` over the two cosets `s ∈ {0, 1}` (the fibre `v^s ⟨ω⟩`) as `Ψ(s) = 8 v^{sk} (1 + λ (v⁸)^s)`, that is `Ψ(0) = 8(1 + λ)` and `Ψ(1) = 8 v^k (1 − λ)` by the half-turn `v⁸ = −1` (`half_turn_sixteen`).

C16.name: FRC.Composite.carrier_641
C16.doc: 22:C16, 22:C17 — the worked carrier `𝔽₆₄₁` (`κ = 160`): `g = 3` is primitive; the Object generator `g_O = g⁴⁰ = 601` has order `16` and `g_O⁸ = −1` (the doublet's sign); the setting step `ζ₈₀ = g⁸ = 151` has order `80`; the octant `ζ₈ = g⁸⁰ = 318` has `ζ₈⁴ = −1`, `(ζ₈ + ζ₈⁷)² = 2` and `S² = 8`; the Bell core is `C₈` (`gcd(40, 16) = 8`).

C17.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.tsirelson
C17.doc: 00:C8, 22:C17, 22:C25, 22:X7, 22:P3 — the Tsirelson square without a generator: `ζ⁴ = −1` gives `(ζ + ζ⁷)² = 2`.

C17.name: FRC.Composite.singlet_square
C17.doc: 22:C17, 22:X7, 22:C25, 22:P3 — the Tsirelson square: `S = 2(ζ + ζ⁷)` for `ζ⁴ = −1` has `S² = 8` on every shell, the shadow of the ring identity `S² = 8` in `ℤ[ζ₈]`.

C17.name: FRC.Composite.no_signalling
C17.doc: 22:C17 — no-signalling: the marginal of one wing, `c(1 + E) + c(1 − E)` over the two outcomes of the other (`c = 1/4`), is `2c`, independent of the correlator and so of the far setting.

C17.name: FRC.Observation.reduce_mul
C17.doc: 22:C9, 22:C17 — the reduction is multiplicative: with `v^n = 1`, the shadow of the convolution `c ⋆ c'` is the product of the shadows; the Carrier-chart amplitude of a product is the product of the amplitudes, exact as algebra.

C17.name: FRC.Composite.carrier_641
C17.doc: 22:C16, 22:C17 — the worked carrier `𝔽₆₄₁` (`κ = 160`): `g = 3` is primitive; the Object generator `g_O = g⁴⁰ = 601` has order `16` and `g_O⁸ = −1` (the doublet's sign); the setting step `ζ₈₀ = g⁸ = 151` has order `80`; the octant `ζ₈ = g⁸⁰ = 318` has `ζ₈⁴ = −1`, `(ζ₈ + ζ₈⁷)² = 2` and `S² = 8`; the Bell core is `C₈` (`gcd(40, 16) = 8`).

C18.name: FRC.Quantum.pair_offset
C18.doc: 00:F2, 00:F6, 22:C26, 22:C15, 22:C18, 22:P3 — two parts of periods `a`, `b` with joint period `T` (a common multiple, and no positive common multiple below it): the number `g` with `g T = a b` divides both periods, and every common divisor divides it (`g` is the gcd); the joint drive carries `(x, y)` to `(x', y')` within one joint period exactly when the offsets agree modulo `g` — the conserved offset on the gcd cycle, the orbits the quotient `A/⟨v⟩ ≅ ℤ/g`.

C18.name: FRC.Composite.cluster_offset
C18.doc: 00:F6, 22:C15, lem:mbody (i)–(ii), 22:C18 — the offset is the orbit label: two configurations `x, y` of the cluster `(ℤ/N)^m` (`0 < m`, `y` reduced) lie on one orbit of the diagonal drive exactly when their offset vectors agree, `x_j − x_0 ≡ y_j − y_0 (mod N)` for every cell `j`; the drive time `t` is a residue, `t < N`, and no drive evolution connects distinct offsets.

C19.name: FRC.Composite.channel_complementarity
C19.doc: 22:C19, 22:P1 — **`V² + C² = 1`** on every shell: for a unit phase `x` with inverse `y`, the visibility `V = (x + y)/2` and the concurrence `C = (x − y)/(2i)` (`h = 1/2`, `i² = −1`, `1/i = −i`) satisfy `V² + C² = 1` exactly, the which-path complementarity of the pure gravitational channel.

C19.name: FRC.Composite.channel_product_at_zero
C19.doc: 22:C19 — at zero coupling the branch state is a product: the concurrence vanishes, `C = h (x − x)(−i) = 0`.

C19.name: FRC.Quantum.channel_chart
C19.doc: 22:C19, 22:P1 [chart] — the channel's chart: `V = cos(φ/2)`, `C = sin(φ/2)`, `V² + C² = 1` (`FRC.Chart.channel_chart`, `Theme/Chart.lean`).

C19.name: FRC.Quantum.channel_entangles
C19.doc: 22:C19 [chart] — the channel entangles off the trivial phase: `sin(φ/2) ≠ 0` for `0 < φ < 2π` (`FRC.Chart.channel_entangles`, `Theme/Chart.lean`).

C20.name: FRC.Composite.drive_norm
C20.doc: 22:C20 — the drive conserves the ledger norm: a unit phase `u` (`u ū = 1`) leaves `a ā` unchanged, so an isolated superposition keeps unit fringe contrast at every drive time.

C20.name: FRC.Composite.revival
C20.doc: 22:C20 — the exact revival: the visibility `V(t) = Σ_E p_E ζ^{E t}` returns to `Σ_E p_E` at the recurrence `n` (`ζ^n = 1`): dephasing, never collapse.

C20.name: FRC.Quantum.joint_recurrence
C20.doc: 00:F2, 22:C26, 22:C10, 22:C20 — the joint recurrence of an unequal-cycle composite, found below a common multiple `L > 0` of the periods (on a shell, a joint return below `Ω`): the chronons at which all `m` parts return are exactly the multiples of one period `T`, `0 < T ≤ L`, which divides `L`. The search never passes `L` (Q20).

C21.name: FRC.Composite.branch_phase
C21.doc: 22:C21 (ii), 22:P1 — the branch phase of `m_c` synchronised cells is the coherent product `ζ^{m_c a}`.

C21.name: FRC.Composite.pair_product
C21.doc: 22:C21 (ii) — the pairwise law: the phase of `m₁` against `m₂` synchronised cells is `ζ^{m₁ m₂ a}`.

C21.name: FRC.Composite.spread_cancels
C21.doc: 22:C21 (iii) — a complete sector sum vanishes: the offset-spread cells' phases cancel over one cycle.

C21.name: FRC.Composite.channel_assembly
C21.doc: 22:C21 (iii), 22:P1 — the reduced channel factorises: the offset distribution's partial sum times the coherent phase, `Σ_θ p_θ ζ^{θ + c} = (Σ_θ p_θ ζ^θ) ζ^c = χ_inc · ζ^{f φ}`.

C22.name: FRC.Composite.field_linear
C22.doc: 22:C22 (i) — the stationary field is linear in its sources with coefficient exactly `m` per locked cluster of `m` cells: `Σ_{i<m} u = m u`.

C22.name: FRC.Composite.eta_zero
C22.doc: 22:C22 (ii) — the exact equivalence-principle null: the pull `m_t ∇u` on a locked test cluster against its inertia `m_t` gives the acceleration `∇u` for every `m_t` (`w = m_t⁻¹`), so `η = 0` identically.

C22.name: FRC.Composite.locked_norm
C22.doc: lem:mbody (iii), 22:C15, 22:C22 — on the synchronised orbit the amplitudes add coherently: `Σ_{i<m} χ = m χ`, and the weight `(m χ)(m χ̄) = m²` when `χ χ̄ = 1`.

C22.name: FRC.Composite.spread_average
C22.doc: lem:mbody (iii), 22:C22, 22:C15 — **the offset-uniform average is `m`**: for `m` cells with independent uniform phases on a cycle of order `n` (`ζ` of order `n`, `η = ζ⁻¹`, neither `1`), the sum over all `n^m` configurations of `|Σ_i ζ^{v_i}|² = (Σ_i ζ^{v_i})(Σ_j η^{v_j})` is `m n^m`, the average `m`, against `m²` on the synchronised orbit: the `√m` lives only in amplitude-coherent observables.

C23.name: FRC.Composite.joint_refinement
C23.doc: 22:C23 (i), 22:X4 — joint refinement: the common cosets of two cores (classes modulo `α` and modulo `β` on the Object cycle) are the classes modulo one period `T`, the common core's, in either order; `T` lies below the product `αβ` (`FRC.Quantum.joint_recurrence` on the two parts, the search bounded by `αβ`).

C23.name: FRC.Composite.order_independence
C23.doc: 22:C23 (ii), 22:X4 — shared-core agreement: with the common core of order `e` dividing both cores `a`, `b`, the channels `r ≡ k (mod a)` of `S` and `r' ≡ k (mod b)` of `S'` agree on the common core, `r ≡ r' (mod e)`: both induce the one character `η_{k mod e}`.

C23.name: FRC.Observation.selection
C23.doc: 00:F4, 00:F6, 22:C4, 22:C23, 22:X3, 22:C24, 22:X5 — the selection rule: a pointer channel `r < d` couples to the Object winding `k` over a fibre of the core exactly when their core phases agree, `k ≡ r (mod d)`: `Σ_{j<d} ω^{kj} ω^{(d−r)j} = d [k ≡ r]`.

C24.name: FRC.Observation.classicality_index
C24.doc: 00:F4, 22:C24, 22:X5 — with the core `C_d` of index `k` in the Object cycle `C_n = C_{dk}`: the Object is absorbed (classical, one outcome per channel) exactly when `k = 1`, that is when its cycle is the core, and resolved (quantum) exactly when `1 < k`, that is when the core is a proper subgroup.

C24.name: FRC.Composite.carrier_421
C24.doc: 22:C24, 22:X5 — the worked carrier `𝔽₄₂₁` (`κ = 105`): `g = 2` is primitive, `I = g^{−105} = g^{315} = 392`, `I² = −1`; the Subject `S₆₁` (`C₆₀`) resolves `O₂₉` (`C₂₈`) through the core `Q₄` (`gcd(60, 28) = 4`) in seven outcomes (`28 = 4 · 7`) and absorbs `O₁₃` (`C₁₂`, `gcd(60, 12) = 12`, one outcome): quantumness is the subgroup index.

C25.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.tsirelson

C25.name: FRC.Composite.singlet_square

C26.name: FRC.Quantum.joint_recurrence
C26.doc: 00:F2, 22:C26, 22:C10, 22:C20 — the joint recurrence of an unequal-cycle composite, found below a common multiple `L > 0` of the periods (on a shell, a joint return below `Ω`): the chronons at which all `m` parts return are exactly the multiples of one period `T`, `0 < T ≤ L`, which divides `L`. The search never passes `L` (Q20).

C26.name: FRC.Quantum.joint_least
C26.doc: 22:C26 — the joint period is the least common multiple: no positive joint return comes earlier.

C26.name: FRC.Quantum.pair_offset
C26.doc: 00:F2, 00:F6, 22:C26, 22:C15, 22:C18, 22:P3 — two parts of periods `a`, `b` with joint period `T` (a common multiple, and no positive common multiple below it): the number `g` with `g T = a b` divides both periods, and every common divisor divides it (`g` is the gcd); the joint drive carries `(x, y)` to `(x', y')` within one joint period exactly when the offsets agree modulo `g` — the conserved offset on the gcd cycle, the orbits the quotient `A/⟨v⟩ ≅ ℤ/g`.

C26.name: FRC.Quantum.dephasing
C26.doc: 00:F2, 00:F6, 22:C26, 22:C7 — dephasing is exact: on a prime shell `q`, a character `χ(x) = Π_j ζ_j^{x_j}` of the composite (`ζ_j^{n_j} = 1`) that the drive moves (`χ(v) = Π_j ζ_j ≠ 1`) sums to zero along the drive, `Σ_{t<M} χ(t v) = 0`, over every joint recurrence `M`, the product of the periods among them.

C26.name: FRC.Composite.winding_period
C26.doc: 00:F6, 22:C26 — the winding `s` on the cycle `C_n` has period `n/gcd(s, n)`: with `n = d n'`, `s = d s'` and `d` the gcd (`s' u = n' v + 1` the Bezout witness of coprimality), the drive `x ↦ x + s` returns, `s t ≡ 0 (mod n)`, exactly when `n' ∣ t`; the joint recurrence of a composite is then the lcm of these periods (`FRC.Quantum.joint_recurrence`).

C27.name: FRC.Observation.transport_trichotomy
C27.doc: 22:C27 — the ambient quarter-turn `g^{−κ} = g^{3κ}` of a shell of capacity `κ` reduces onto an embedded label `C_n`, `n = 4m` dividing `4κ` (`κ = m t`), generated by `ζ`, as `ζ^{3κ}`: it is the label's own quarter-turn `ζ^{3m}` (faithful) exactly when `κ ≡ m (mod n)`, its conjugate `ζ^m` exactly when `κ + m ≡ 0 (mod n)`, and a sign (broken, no quarter-turn: its square is `1`) exactly when `κ ≡ 0 (mod n/2)`, the complement of the two quarter-turn cases; for `n = 4` the three cases are `κ ≡ 1`, `κ ≡ 3` and `κ` even, the residue mod `4`; on `C_{40}` the broken case is `κ ≡ 0 (mod 20)`, the `𝔽_{641}` case (`κ = 160`). C27.name: FRC.Observation.transport_cases
C27.doc: 22:C27 — the three cases read on the capacity, decided by the kernel on the worked labels `C_{40}`, `Q₄` and `C_{12}`: `3κ ≡ 3m`, `3κ ≡ m` and `6κ ≡ 0 (mod 4m)` are `κ ≡ m`, `κ + m ≡ 0` and `κ ≡ 0 (mod 2m)`, and on `C_{12}` (`m = 3`, the embedded capacities `κ = 3t`) the faithful case is `κ ≡ 3 (mod 12)`.

C28.name: FRC.Strata.Q2.pow_Wp_irrational
C28.doc: 22:C28 — `(2 + √2)^{m+1}` is irrational for every `m`: the agreeing Tsirelson weight raised to any positive power is no realised tally.

C28.name: FRC.Strata.Q2.string_rational_iff_box
C28.doc: 22:C28 — on the box `a, b < 13` the string weight `W₊^a W₋^b` is a rational integer exactly when the string is balanced, `a = b`; the unbounded statement follows from `pow_Wp_irrational` and `W₊ W₋ = 2`.

C28.name: FRC.Strata.Q2.trace_rational
C28.doc: 22:C28 — the Galois trace `x + x̄` is rational for every `x`: a string summed with its conjugate-setting string is a tally.

C28.name: FRC.Strata.Q2.Wp_mul_Wm
C28.doc: 22:C28 — `W₊ W₋ = (2 + √2)(2 − √2) = 2`: an agreeing and a disagreeing pair cancel to the tally `2`.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.Readout.cells_all_settings
C29.doc: 22:C29 — at scale `n = 4` every setting's integer part is certified by its isolating polynomial: `s₄(Δ)` is the grid cell of the root `c_Δ` for all 80 settings, decided by the kernel on the homogenised integers.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.Readout.cells_P20
C29.doc: 22:C29 — the cells of `P₂₀` on the grid of scale `81` over `[−2, 2]`: exactly the twenty integer parts of the odd settings, one cell per root and no cell holding two — the finite isolation of all twenty roots.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.Readout.pair_sum
C29.doc: 22:C29 — the readout pair of a setting, numerators over the denominator `bG`: the two weights `(u ± c)/b` share the integer part `s` of `Gc`, so their readouts sum to `2u/b` exactly, on counts: `(uG + s) + (uG − s) = uG + uG`.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.hamilton_count
C29.doc: 22:C29 — the bounded-discrepancy law: for a readout `a/D` and `B` runs the provisional count `f = ⌊B a / D⌋` exists with `B a = D f + (B a mod D)`, and with any residual unit `δ ≤ 1` the registered count `f + δ` lies within one of `B a/D`.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.Readout.tsirelson_restriction
C29.doc: 22:C29 — restriction: at the Tsirelson setting the cell certificate of `X² − 2` is the two-sided bound of the integer square root of `2 · 81²`, `114² ≤ 2 · 81² < 115²` (`s₄ = 114`), and the readout numerators are `2 · 81 ± 114 = 276, 48` over `8 · 81 = 648`: the paper's `23/54` and `2/27`.

C29.name: FRC.Strata.Readout.classical_exact
C29.doc: 22:C29 — the four classical settings read exactly: the cell is the exact point `Gc` (`hom = 0`), the readout is the weight.
